newsitem.title: GERMANY: German intervention grain offers remain low.
newsitem.headline: German intervention grain offers remain low.

text.p: Sales offers into German grain intervention stores in the November-May 1996/97 season totalled 203,151 tonnes by November 22, compared with 889,423 a year earlier, state grain intervention board BLE said on Monday.
The figures include volumes accepted, but not yet delivered to stores, by the close last Friday.

Traders said market prices of grain in most regions were above the November buying-in level of 231.49 marks per tonne and that sellers were seeking to place wheat and rye in the free market, but sales were slow.
Barley and feed rye prices, however, were beginning to get nearer to the intervention level, especially as newly harvested maize was competing in feed markets.
Barley and rye sales into intervention were mostly noted in northern and eastern Germany.
